entries.pronunciation note: weak /nəmˈsɛlf/ · nuhm-SELF — one consonant from the reduced themself and emself, both /əmˈsɛlf/, so in connected speech the three sit very close together
entries.русский: неологизм, русского эквивалента нет — возвратное набора ne/nem/nir
entries.register: neutral among the speakers who use the set, and rare in general American writing — the reflexive of the ne / nem / nir / nirs set, listed on pronoun-reference sites since the early 2010s and used by a small number of speakers. The subject ne is said /ni/, "nee", and the possessive nir /nɪr/, "neer".
entries.refers to: one person who uses the ne set, named in the same clause. The licensing is ordinary reflexive licensing — no different from herself needing its she.
entries.agreement: ne takes a singular verb — ne is in the lab, ne was hired in March, ne has two kids. The reflexive is -self, never -selves.
entries.pattern: ne [verb] nemself · ne [verb] [preposition] nemself · [NP] nemself [verb] · by nemself
entries.variants: nirself /nɪrˈsɛlf/ · neer-SELF, built on the possessive nir rather than the object nem. Both are in use and speakers differ on which they take, the same split xemself shows against xyrself and emself against eirself, and structurally the same as standard themself (object base) against vernacular theirself (possessive base) — with the difference that neither ne-form carries stigma.
entries.contrast: Against emself: the two sets build the reflexive the same way, object form plus -self, and the results differ by an initial /n/ that fast speech does little to protect. Against xemself and zirself: separate sets whose object forms rhyme with this one. Against aerself, coself, faerself, hirself, perself, and verself: separate sets again, not substitutes. Against themself: singular both, but ne takes a singular verb where singular they takes a plural one.
entries.see also: emself, aerself, coself, faerself, xemself, themself, ne / nem

entries.meaning: The reflexive of the per set, the one neopronoun built by cutting down an existing English noun rather than by inventing a syllable — which is why it reads as plain, and why it turns up in fiction earlier and more often than in style guides.
examples: Per taught perself to weld the summer after graduation. (1)
Per gave perself an extra week on the manuscript. (1)
Per has never thought of perself as a teacher. (1)
Per rebuilt the deck perself, start to finish. (2)
The author perself answered the letter. (2)
Per spent the whole holiday by perself and came back rested. (3)
Per kept the results to perself until the lab confirmed them. (3)

entries.register: neutral among the speakers who use the set, and rare in general American writing — the reflexive of the per / per / pers set, clipped from person — coined by Marge Piercy in the 1976 novel Woman on the Edge of Time and used since by a small number of speakers, chiefly people who prefer a form built out of an ordinary English word
entries.refers to: one person who uses the per set, named in the same clause
entries.agreement: per takes a singular verb — per is here, per has signed. Note that per is the same word in the subject and object slots (per called, I called per), the way you is, so the reflexive perself and the possessive pers are the only separate forms in the set.
entries.pattern: per [verb] perself · per [verb] [preposition] perself · [NP] perself [verb] · by perself
entries.contrast: Against herself: the two differ by one consonant, and in a noisy room the pair is easy to mishear, which is worth knowing before assuming a speaker misspoke. Against emself, hirself, verself, xemself, and zirself: separate sets, not substitutes. And against the ordinary preposition per (per the contract, sixty per hour), a spelling collision that makes this set harder to search for than the others.
entries.see also: emself, hirself, verself, xemself, zirself, aerself, coself, faerself, nemself, themself, oneself

Ve does not consider verself retired. (1)
Ve ran the entire simulation verself. (2)
The pilot verself signed off on the repair. (2)
Ve went out to the ridge by verself before dawn. (3)
Ve kept the finding to verself until the review was over. (3)

entries.meaning: The reflexive of the xe set, the most visible of the neopronouns in current American use and the one most often mispronounced on first meeting, because English gives word-initial x- the /z/ of xylophone.
examples: Xe taught xemself to code between shifts. (1)
Xe gave xemself a week off after the deadline. (1)
Xe doesn't count xemself among the optimists. (1)
Xe painted the whole apartment xemself. (2)
The director xemself stayed for the entire rehearsal. (2)
Xe flew out to the conference by xemself. (3)
Xe kept the offer to xemself until the contract was signed. (3)
Xe found xyrself explaining the forms all morning. (1; the possessive-base variant)

entries.русский: неологизм, русского эквивалента нет — возвратное набора xe/xem/xyr
entries.register: neutral among the speakers who use the set, and rare in general American writing — the reflexive of the xe / xem / xyr / xyrs set, in circulation since at least the 1970s and the most frequently cited of the neopronoun sets online since the 2010s
entries.refers to: one person who uses the xe set, named in the same clause
entries.agreement: xe takes a singular verb — xe is presenting, xe was hired in June
entries.pattern: xe [verb] xemself · xe [verb] [preposition] xemself · [NP] xemself [verb] · by xemself
entries.variants: xyrself /zɪrˈsɛlf/ · zeer-SELF, built on the possessive xyr instead of the object xem. Both are in use and speakers differ; the split is structurally the same as standard themself (object base) against vernacular theirself (possessive base), with neither xe-form stigmatized. Some writers spell the possessive xer, which gives xerself.
entries.contrast: Against zirself: different sets that sound alike — /zɛm/ against /zɪr/ — and the reflexive is often the word that shows which set is meant. Against themself: both singular, but xe takes a singular verb where singular they takes a plural one. The trap in this entry is the spelling rather than the grammar: xe, xem, and xyr all open with /z/.

entries.register: neutral among the speakers who use the set, and rare in general American writing — the reflexive of the ze (also spelled zie) / zir / zirs set, the most used of the z- sets in current American writing
entries.refers to: one person who uses the ze/zir set, named in the same clause. Zir is both the object form and the possessive determiner (I met zir, zir brother), so like hirself the reflexive has a single base.
entries.agreement: ze takes a singular verb — ze is in the studio, ze has already left

entries.variants: zerself, matching the spelling zer used by speakers who pronounce the vowel that way. The subject pronoun ze also heads the older ze/hir set, whose reflexive is hirself — same subject, different object base, and the reflexive is what tells them apart.
entries.contrast: Against hirself: the two share the subject ze, and only the object and possessive forms differ. Against xemself: a near-neighbor in sound, /zɪr/ against /zɛm/, and a separate set.
